title: Truth in Lending (Regulation Z)
summary: The Board and the Bureau (collectively, Agencies) are publishing final rules amending the official interpretations for the Agencies' regulations that implement the Truth in Lending Act (TILA). The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Dodd- Frank Act) amended TILA to require that the dollar threshold for exempt consumer credit transactions be adjusted annually by the annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the annual percentage increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $73,400 to $76,300 effective January 1, 2027. Because the Dodd- Frank Act also requires similar adjustments in the Consumer Leasing Act's threshold for exempt consumer leases, the Agencies are making similar amendments to each of their respective regulations implementing the Consumer Leasing Act elsewhere in the Rules section of this issue of the Federal Register.

title: Consumer Leasing (Regulation M)
summary: The Board and the Bureau (collectively, Agencies) are finalizing amendments to the official interpretations for the Agencies' regulations that implement the Consumer Leasing Act (CLA). The Dodd- Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Dodd-Frank Act) amended the CLA to require that the dollar threshold for exempt consumer leases be adjusted annually by the annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the annual percentage increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $73,400 to $76,300, effective January 1, 2027. Because the Dodd-Frank Act also requires similar adjustments in the Truth in Lending Act's threshold for exempt consumer credit transactions, the Agencies are making similar amendments to each of their respective regulations implementing the Truth in Lending Act elsewhere in the Rules section of this issue of the Federal Register.

title: Appraisals for Higher-Priced Mortgage Loans Exemption Threshold
summary: The OCC, the Board, and the Bureau are finalizing amendments to the official interpretations for their regulations that implement section 129H of the Truth in Lending Act (TILA). Section 129H of TILA establishes special appraisal requirements for "higher-risk mortgages," termed "higher-priced mortgage loans" or "HPMLs" in the agencies' regulations. The regulations provide that transactions of $25,000 or less are exempt from these requirements, adjusted annually based on any annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the CPI-W in effect as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $34,200 to $35,500, effective January 1, 2027.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status for Streaked Horned Lark With a Section 4(d) Rule
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the streaked horned lark (Eremophila alpestris strigata), a subspecies of grassland songbird from Oregon and Washington, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would maintain the species as a threatened species on the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and continue to extend the Act's protections to the species.

summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the piebald madtom (Noturus gladiator), a fish species from Mississippi and Tennessee, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the piebald madtom. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species.

Agency Information Collection Activities; 30 CFR 764-State Processes for Designating Areas Unsuitable for Surface Coal Mining Operations
summary: In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSM) is proposing to renew an information collection. The information collection allows individuals and other interested parties to petition State regulatory authorities to designate lands as unsuitable for surface coal mining operations or to terminate an existing designation. The information is used by State regulatory authorities to evaluate and process petitions in accordance with the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (SMCRA).

title: Proposed Withdrawal Extension and Opportunity for Public Meeting for the Sugarloaf Petroglyphs and Pine Spring Archeological Sites, Wyoming
summary: The Secretary of the Interior proposes to extend Public Land Order (PLO) No. 6650, as extended by PLO No. 7678, for an additional 20-year term. PLO No. 6650, as extended, withdrew 20 acres of public lands, subject to valid existing rights, from settlement, sale, location, or entry under the general land laws, including the United States mining laws, but not from leasing under the mineral leasing laws, to protect the educational, scientific, and artistic values as well as the capital investment for Sugarloaf Petroglyphs and Pine Spring Archeological Sites in Sweetwater County, Wyoming. This Notice advises the public of an opportunity to comment on the proposed withdrawal extension and to request a public meeting.
